short: A new dark-fantasy Task Bar idle RPG. Six heroes, twelve specializations and hordes that fight back — right above your taskbar while you work. Loot, upgrade, rebirth. Free to play, with Steam Community Market trading planned after launch.
about: A new Task Bar RPG — with a real economy  Task Bar Dungeons  is a new dark-fantasy idle RPG in a compact window in the corner of your screen. Three heroes fight endless hordes on their own. You pick the team, the skills and the builds — and after launch, you'll trade what you find on the Steam Community Market. We don't hunt bots. We make botting pointless.       Trading games usually lose the war against gold farms. Ours was built from day one so that farming simply doesn't pay.    Smart loot system  — keep the best, trade the rest.    No invasive anti-cheat, no random bans.     An economy that stays fair  — Steam Market trading arrives in a later update, not on launch day.    Every hero can be earned  — DLC is a shortcut, never the only way.         Everything in a DLC can also be earned in-game — through quests, crafting and secret challenges. It takes time, but everyone plays on equal terms. Buying the DLC supports us and skips the wait — with our thanks. We respect every choice. Story Mode     Yes, there are a lot of “Task Bar” games right now. That doesn't mean ours has to be empty.  We make Task Bar Dungeons because we love RPGs and idle games, and we wanted an RPG you can truly enjoy without sitting in front of the screen for hours. That's why we're actively working on a story mode: a world to dive into, heroes worth getting to know, and a plot you'll actually want to follow.   Wait, wait! If you're just here to level up and farm:  the whole story turns off with one button. Just your party and the loot.  On top of that, we'll regularly release  comics  and  interactive visual novels  about our heroes, the lore and the story. All free, simply because we love the world we've built. A new hero every month After launch we plan to add a new hero every month: new specializations, new skills, new ways to break your party build. Plays while you work Put it in the corner and get on with your day. Collapse the window to just the battle, or pin it on top. Your party fights, levels up and picks up loot on its own — even while you Alt-Tab into work — and keeps going while the game is closed, for up to 8 hours.   A meeting drags on. In the corner of your screen, Noxa pulls a whole pack of Drowned Guards into a black hole.  And if you want to go deeper… …we're not telling. Not yet. We'd rather show you on first launch. Just know this: there's more to do here than on your actual to-do list. Six heroes. Twelve ways to play. Every hero has two specializations, and one switch changes everything: weapon, skills, role in the party. Each specialization brings four skills, its own passive and its own talent tree — 15 nodes and 4 skill upgrades. Take your heroes to level 100, rebirth them for permanent bonuses and build the party nobody else thought of.   VARG  · Living Shield / Heavy Crossbowman     Varg is raw beastly power you can trust with your party. A hulking werewolf, a predator's grin and weapons that match his size: when he steps forward, even the darkness gives ground.   MARA  · Guardian / Healer     Mara brings calm to the moment before the hardest blow. A knight of steel resolve and a steady gaze, she makes the darkest dungeon feel like a place your party can survive.   ROOK  · Marksman / Beast Master     A quiet hunter with a cool gaze and a loyal bear at his side. There is something dangerous in Rook's stillness: he has already chosen his target.   SERA  · Battle Mage / Fire Summoner     Sera walks into darkness as though it were her stage. A daring smile, fire at her fingertips and a blazing temper — every descent becomes a spectacle in her company.   REYNA  · Kunai Skirmisher / Blade Dancer ·  Supporter Pack      Quick, bold and dangerously charming. Reyna turns combat into a dance along a blade's edge, with an easy smile and steel that moves faster than the eye can follow.   NOXA  · Abyss Witch / Dawnkeeper ·  Supporter Pack      Noxa draws you to the boundary between abyss and dawn. In darkness she is cold and commanding;

lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Danish, Ukrainian, Russian, Bulgarian, Hungarian, Indonesian, Turkish, Greek, Norwegian, Czech, Japanese, Polish, Thai, Swedish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Romanian, Finnish, Dutch, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Spanish - Latin America, Vietnamese, Korean, Malay
short: Turn your desktop into a self-running astral alchemy workshop. Typing gathers Stardust to fuel the forge. Return to experiment, craft mysterious creations, collect rare relics, handle surprise events, and exchange supplies, items, and greetings with other alchemists asynchronously.
about: Welcome to Astral Forge!           Demo Note: This demo focuses on Astral Forge's core desktop operation, Stardust progression, alchemy, and collection experience. Some asynchronous exchange, Steam Inventory, long-term progression, workshop events, and expanded features are still in development and testing; some features described below may not be enabled in the demo.      Turn Your Desktop into an Astral Alchemy Workshop That Keeps Running    Astral Forge: Desktop Alchemist   is a living astral alchemy world designed to run beside your everyday PC use.  As you type and use your computer, you gradually gather  Stardust . These resources keep the workshop moving and prepare the way for your next alchemy experiment.  When you are busy, let it keep growing beside you.  When you have time, come back and light the forge again.     Typing → Stardust → Alchemy → Reveal → Collect                Actually Perform an Alchemy Experiment   The forge is the heart of the workshop.  Choose materials, prepare an experiment, watch the heat and changing conditions, and decide when to commit to the forge.  The result is not simply placed in front of you before the process begins.  The fun is in wondering:   What will this experiment create?   A new material, a mysterious creation, a new compendium entry, or something much rarer may be waiting after the next experiment.            Forge, Discover, Collect   Experimenting brings more materials, mysterious creations, relics, and collectibles.  Start with common discoveries, gradually fill unknown compendium entries, and keep searching for rarer results.  Growing your workshop is not just about making a number bigger.  You can actually see:   what you have discovered along the way.                The Workshop Is Not Always Quiet   An idle alchemy workshop does not stay peaceful forever.  Occasionally, workshop events appear and ask for your attention.  For example:  a dangerous bomb may suddenly show up.  Notice it early and click in time:  Defused.  Miss it and…  BOOM.  These little unexpected events keep the workshop from feeling like a looping alchemy animation on your desktop.  Even when you are not staring at it, something can actually happen in this world.  …             A Workshop That Keeps Becoming More Complete   The forge is only the center of the world.  As you progress, collections, functional areas, different devices, material systems, and other mechanics gradually form a more complete astral workshop.  Sometimes you return for another experiment.  Sometimes you manage your collection.  Sometimes you handle an unexpected event.  And sometimes you do nothing at all and simply let the world keep running beside you.               Play at Your Own Pace Without Being Completely Alone   Astral Forge also includes light asynchronous player interaction.  You do not need to join a real-time multiplayer room, and both players do not need to be online at the same time.  Through asynchronous systems, you can send or receive  basic supplies, greetings, and selected items,  so your workshop can keep its own pace while still forming light connections with other alchemists.  Asynchronous exchanges prioritize added friends; when no suitable friend is available, the system can match other players, with a fallback mechanism to keep the process moving.  No endlessly scrolling public chat, and no pressure from real-time multiplayer.  At some unexpected moment, you may simply receive a bundle of supplies, an item, or a greeting from another alchemist far away.            Rare Discoveries & Steam Collectibles   Alchemy and exploration can also lead to more unusual discoveries.  Some special items can enter your  Steam Inventory , letting part of your collection live beyond the save file itself.  You can keep your collection long term; items that support market trading can also be traded with other players through the Steam Community Market.  That means some special discoveries can truly become part of y

lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Hatch a little dragon on your desktop! Feed it, teach it new skills, and send it exploring. Meals are on you, but idle treasure chests can help! Meet the locals, rebuild their village, and see what you and your dragon discover together.
about: At first, I just wanted something on my desktop to keep me company while I coded. And that’s how a little dragon that could walk around and fly across my screen came to be.  Then I thought: I spend every day reading research papers—could my dragon get stronger, too? So I gave it things to study and places to explore.  Later, I thought,   “This game is getting really fun!”   Could I share that fun with   friends  ? So dragons learned to visit each other! And  after getting judged for showing up empty-handed,  they can now bring gifts!  More and more friends were joining in! But whose dragon was stronger? Naturally, the dragons needed a way to   challenge each other  !          While exploring, I found myself with nothing much to do… so I opened a certain deckbuilding roguelike. Then I thought: why can’t my dragon play one, too?  Having two games open while sneaking in a little gaming time felt a bit risky … And that’s how   roguelike tower climbing   found its way into the Endless Tower!  One little dragon seemed a bit lonely. Could it have even littler dragons to keep it company? And so,   hatching baby dragons   became a thing!  Then I thought: wouldn’t it be cool if my dragon could dress up? And suddenly I was making art for   outfits, hats, and wings  …  What could all these dragons do together…? Well, now they can run their own   farm   and   restaurant  !  Oh, and there’s more…          I’ve played a lot of games over the years. Many of the ones I loved have since disappeared, which always feels like such a shame. Could I bring a little of what I loved about them back through my dragons? (Of course, this little dragon game isn’t exactly a AAA production…)  I’m pretty sure some of the anime I watched as a kid found their way into the game, too. If you’ve guessed which ones—yep, probably those. The ones where a little companion grows alongside the main character.  Oh, right! I’ve also hidden lots of   Easter eggs  ! And I want to add even more!    The full version is already finished!   I’m now busy polishing things up and working on optimizations—trying very hard not to get distracted. If all goes well, it should be out in November.     And… thank you for playing my game.     Hmm… that’s all for now!

name: River Whisker
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Ukrainian, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Polish, Thai, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Spanish - Latin America, Korean
short: A little painted riverbank in the corner of your screen, where cats wander over while you work. An angler fishes, the cats get a share, and you can pet each one and give it a name. Nothing to tend, even while you're away.
about: A desktop companion game for the corner of your screen: a hand-painted riverbank, an angler, and nine cats who get to know you, little by little.           While you're busy, there's a small riverbank in a corner of your screen, and someone sitting on it, quietly keeping you company as you work. When you're tired and look up, the water is flowing, doves lift from the bell tower, and a distant bell rings the hour. One by one, the fish go into the basket, and cats begin to come by. Nine cats who get to know you "They sat by my chair, a hand's span from my shoe, so I cast with my arm a little lower." Six cats come by the basket for fish, each with their own temper and favourite fish. One usually sits down to wash their face after eating; one sleeps so deeply that a landed fish often doesn't wake them. Three more come only in special weather. The rainy-day one wears a green cloak and carries a gourd; who comes in the snow or the heat is yours to find out. When your hand rests on a friend, they lean toward you. The name you give is the one they keep, and every first time they eat, nap or sit by the stove is kept on their page of moments.         Nothing to look after No one goes hungry or falls ill, there are no daily chores, and a cat who knows you never forgets you. While you're away, the bank carries on; when you come back, the journal tells you who came by and who slept a while in the grass. A first meeting waits until you're back. No gacha, no real-money purchases, and no cat is ever bought or sold.         Your hours, tonight's moon The light follows your computer's clock: mist in the morning, windows lighting up one by one at dusk. The church bell strikes the hour from 7 am to 10 pm and keeps quiet at night.  The moon at night is the same one outside your window; rain, snow and hot days are the riverbank's own weather. A glimpse behind the scenes: the riverbank, coming together bit by bit.         Quiet in its corner Bottom-left or bottom-right, on whichever screen you like. Three sizes; it can stay always on top, or fade while the mouse is elsewhere. When you want a clear screen, it tucks into the tray, and one click brings it back. In the corner it draws fewer frames, so it asks less of your computer. To see the cats up close, a click on the tent unrolls the whole painting.         Fishing, if you feel like it The angler fishes on their own. When the float dips, you can reel in yourself; a ★ fresh fish is the cats' favourite. After a meal, a cat leaves a few coins behind. A yellow catfish, brought up out of the water, gives a soft little croak.         Little things the cats use The cats' coins buy a cushion, a pot of wildflowers, a little tea stove. Cats rest on the cushion and warm themselves by the stove; with plants out, they come by a little more often. A cardboard box for a cat to hop into and doze in, chin on the rim, and a flat stone to nap on. On rainy days, a cat may curl up in the dry patch under the oil-paper umbrella; in the heat, one stretches out on the bamboo mat. After a sniff of catnip, some cats roll over right where they are, and when a butterfly drifts close, a cat may crouch low and watch it for a long while. The water's edge comes alive too: a kingfisher lands on the tip of the propped pole, a pair of wild ducks doze beside the raft, and at dusk or in the rain a frog hops up onto the lotus leaves.           To be clear  Nine cats, twenty kinds of fish, three rods, seventeen pieces of decor (and three more the river brings), and seventy-five first moments to come across, little by little. It's a quiet companion, not a management game: nothing to run, and no numbers to chase.   FAQ    Does the riverbank follow my weather? Rain and snow are the riverbank's own; the light follows your clock, and the moon follows the real calendar.

name: Sumeru Divine Endeavor Demo
lang: English, Simplified Chinese*, Traditional Chinese**
short: Try Sumeru Divine Endeavor, a cultivation and sect management game with no need for constant clicking. Recruit disciples, master mystical arts, collect treasures and forge bonds. Cultivate quietly on your desktop, or switch to immersive mode to focus on your sect.
about: A companion on your desktop. An immortal world to lose yourself in.   This is the demo version of Sumeru Divine Endeavor, a cultivation game about the pursuit of immortality, offering varied activities and deep progression without demanding constant input.  We wanted to find a more relaxed way to play, somewhere between exhausting micromanagement and simply waiting for progress. When life gets busy, the game needs little attention; when you have time to spare, meaningful choices and discoveries await. Enjoy the freedom of playing on your own, while crossing paths with other players who bring companionship to your journey.  Manage a sect, nurture disciples, study cultivation manuals, and collect rare treasures. Or take the demonic path, devoting everything to your Sect Leader's own advancement. In this world, the path you follow is yours to choose.       A Desktop Companion, a World to Immerse Yourself In  Give this world of cultivation a corner of your desktop, and let the daily life of your sect accompany your work, study, and rest. Focus on what you need to do, then return when you have a moment to check on progress, make plans, and enjoy the growth you've built little by little.  When you're ready for a longer session, switch to immersive mode. Take in your domain, tend to cultivation and management, follow the relationships between its people, and explore more of what the game has to offer.       A brief break or an evening of focused play can both become part of your immortal journey.  Raise a Sect, or Pursue Your Own Ascension  Become a dedicated Sect Leader: recruit disciples, guide them according to their talents, and equip them with cultivation manuals and gear. Build a sect filled with capable cultivators, and enjoy the satisfaction of watching your disciples flourish and your teachings endure.       Or focus on the Sect Leader alone, pursuing your own cultivation and power, even taking the demonic path of refining people into elixirs and commanding corpse puppets. Your disciples' growth and your sect's prosperity need not be your only ambitions.       Forbidden arts carry consequences. Demonic deeds accumulate Evil and draw the wrath of the Righteous Alliance. How you gain your power will shape the reckoning you must face.  Will you shelter an entire sect, or dedicate everything to one cultivator's rise? The choice is yours.       A Wealth of Characters, Spirit Beasts, and Rare Treasures  We've filled this cultivation world with a vast array of characters, Spirit Beasts, Artifacts, and Divine Weapons, each with its own appearance and character, alongside a rich selection of Cultivation Manuals and Immortal Arts. Collecting, nurturing, and finding combinations can become lasting pleasures of their own.            Meet new people, seek out your favorite Spirit Beasts, gather Artifacts and Divine Weapons that suit your needs, and study the ways of cultivation. As you advance through the Realms and gain experience, a wider world will open before you.            If you love characters, explore their histories and relationships. If you love collecting, steadily build your trove. If you enjoy experimenting, spend your time shaping progression and assembling combat combinations.            Every new encounter and every rare find could be the beginning of your next chapter.  Practice the Arts of Cultivation, Build a Domain of Your Own  The pleasures of cultivation also lie in everyday life.       Develop your domain, grow spiritual plants, fish for spirit fish, and refine elixirs to build your sect's resources. Put the fruits of that work into character growth, equipment, and new expeditions, connecting each pursuit to the next.            Think carefully about every resource, or begin with the activities you enjoy most. Tend the herb garden today, study a cultivation manual tomorrow, and venture into a secret realm when you have time.            With patient care, the world before you will come to bear your mark. name: SOME: Space Overlay Mining Empire
lang: English
short: Looking for SOME game right on your desktop that doesn't hijack your monitors? A space station in a corner of your screen, mining ships that cut asteroids apart block by block and haul the ore home, and upgrades that let the fleet run itself while you pretend to work.
about: "What are you playing?"    "Oh, just SOME Space Overlay Mining Empire."     SOME plays right on your desktop, over your other windows. A space station sits in one corner of your screen. Your mining ship flies out to the asteroids around it, cuts them apart block by block with its laser and hauls the ore home. Clicks on empty space go through to the windows underneath, so you keep working while it mines.    From the first click to a fleet that runs itself  At first every trip is yours: click an asteroid to send the ship out, click the full ship to call it home, then unload its cargo and sell the ore. Credits buy lasers, cargo and thrusters, and then the upgrades that take the clicks away: autopilot flies the trips, auto-target picks the next asteroid and auto-unload empties a docked ship. Buy more ships and they work the belts side by side, while you look over now and then to see what they have brought in.    A station built from blocks  The station, the ships and the asteroids are all made of blocks. Every part you buy shows on its ship, and every block you research for the station takes its place there. The tech tree opens over the desktop as a circuit board, rooted in the station's corner, with:    scanners that open the next belt of asteroids and zoom the field out    cranes and a second dock, so the fleet unloads faster    a Refinery that turns ore into material, and an Alloy furnace that makes alloy from crystal and material    a Shipyard, where you lay out each ship's parts on its hull and fit out haulers that fetch the ore your miners drop, so the miners keep cutting    Rearrange the station's blocks at any time, for free: a fitting works only beside its machine.    Past the last belt  Four belts of asteroids ring the station, each further out and richer in crystal than the one before. Open them all and build the jump gate. It joins your station to the galaxy, and a jump takes the station, the fleet and everything you have researched to another system, with rocks of its own and a twist of its own. The game goes on after the gate for as long as you like.    Made to sit beside your work    Pick the corner the station sits in, and the screen, when you have more than one.    Set the game's size from 75 to 200 %, and fade it down to 20 % to let the desktop show through.    It draws at most 30 frames a second, and stops drawing while nothing moves.    Once the fleet runs itself, it keeps mining while the game is closed, for up to eight hours.      Everyone needs SOME Space Overlay Mining Empire.

short: A free-to-play hack-and-slash that fights on in your taskbar. Chibi heroes meet the enemy inside a thin strip at the bottom of your screen. All you do is swap the gear they picked up and respec their skills when you feel like it. No connection needed; the rest happens in the corner of your screen.
about: About this demo This demo covers the first difficulty layer only. More layers will be added to the base game as free updates. A hack-and-slash that fights on in your taskbar Chibi heroes meet the enemy inside a thin strip. They kill it, gear drops, the next one comes. It runs whether you touch it or not. When you feel like it, open the dashboard and swap what fell. That is all there is to it.        Free to play The base game is free. It will not be pay to win. There are no ads. No connection needed. It runs the same either way. There is no server, and no account to create. Pull the plug and nothing changes. No "servers are down today," and no day when the service ends and your save stops working. Yokai leak onto your desktop Now and then the ward slips and one gets out. It steps off the strip, walks the edge of your taskbar, and wanders across your desktop. Click it and it leaves something behind. Ignore it and it finds its own way back.        Anywhere you want it, any size you want    Thin enough to sit over your taskbar — and you can put it anywhere else on screen too    You can resize it. Tuck it small into a corner, or blow it up and watch    Multiple monitors? Drag it across them    The dashboard opens only when you want it. Combat keeps going while it is closed         Melt it. Forge it. Link it. Ten equipment slots: Main Weapon, Sub Weapon, Helm, Body Armor, Bracers, Greaves, two Rings, Amulet and Charm. What rolls on them is random. Nothing you pick up goes to waste.     Salvage  — break gear you don't want down into materials. Hang the right ema and low-rarity drops melt down the moment they fall, without ever touching your bag     Craft  — forge new gear from what you saved. What comes out is not left to chance     Link  — slot magatama (red for Might, blue for Arts, green for Life, yellow for Fortune) into your gear. Three of the same color and rank fuse into one of the next rank. Slotting and unslotting are free.      One stat is never enough Cut your attack interval and it means nothing if each hit is light. Raise your crit rate and it means nothing while your crit damage stays where it was. Stack HP and you still fall if the incoming damage outpaces it. Power here shows up only when two or more things that are insufficient alone start meshing. Your gear screen always shows three totals —  DPS, Sustain and Power . That is where you find out what isn't meshing. Three layers decide your build     Emaki (skill tree)  — a fork at every milestone: sharpen a skill, or change how it behaves. Widen your reach, or narrow it to a point. At the growth choices on Lv10 and Lv25 you pick one of three branches. Respec is always free     Ema Board  — permanent upgrades bought with Merit, earned once for every stage you clear for the first time: experience, drop rates, inventory space, even new party members. Whatever you buy keeps working forever     Vessels  — keep a character deployed and fighting, and the passive that belongs to them alone wakes up in stages   Vessels — hand a woken passive to someone else Once a character's vessel wakes, they can lend a copy of that passive to one other character. The owner loses nothing by lending it. Whose vessel goes to whom? You can raise a character on the bench and send nothing but their vessel to the front. Once your three are picked, there is still a layer left to build. Sigils — what the late game is about Only Legendary gear carries a unique effect. That is its sigil, shown as a single kanji. Finding a Legendary stops being the goal. Finding the one with the sigil you want takes its place. A sigil you like can be pulled out of the gear, recorded, and imprinted onto something else. Bosses Every area ends with the thing that rules it. Mid-bosses turn up along the way, and a key opens the door to something else.        COMBO Every kill pushes your COMBO up; stop killing and it decays. While it climbs, the gear that drops gets better and the enemies themselves spawn faster.

name: AIvy
lang: English*, French*, Italian*, German*, Spanish - Spain*, Portuguese - Portugal*, Russian*, Simplified Chinese*, Traditional Chinese*, Japanese*, Korean**
short: AIvy is a desktop mascot — a 3D character that talks to you naturally, powered by AI. Load your favorite VRM model, and watch it watch over your work, chime in softly, and feel like it's really there. Conversation and voice run entirely on your PC, no account needed.
about: What is AIvy?  AIvy is a desktop mascot that brings a 3D character to your PC desktop—one you can actually talk to, powered by AI. Load your favorite VRM model and watch it come to life in the corner of your screen, chatting naturally like a companion who's really there. The name comes from "AI + ivy"—the gentle vine that quietly winds itself around your everyday life.  Build Your Own Companion, Your Way  The heart of AIvy is the freedom to combine the look, the mind, the voice, and the personality—piece by piece—to craft a companion that's truly yours.  Any VRM works: one you bought on a storefront, one you built yourself in VRoid Studio, or one from VRoid Hub. VRoid Hub integration shows each model's usage terms (avatar use, modification, redistribution, commercial use) for your consent before downloading. Files can also stay where they are and be referenced without copying them into the library.  Loading a model is only the start. Swap to alternate textures bundled with the model, toggle individual parts on and off, map the model's own expressions onto AIvy's emotions, set the idle expression, and tune lighting (ambient and directional intensity, direction, color)—all saved per model. There is also a  beta feature  for outfit swapping: load .unitypackage outfit assets, the format sold on storefronts, straight onto your model (outfits authored for the same base body).  Personality and speech style can be set from ready-made presets, or written freely in your own words to shape every nuance. You can also pick how it responds—empathetic, balanced, or candid—so your companion isn't just a yes-machine.  With support for 11 languages including Japanese, English, Chinese, and Korean, people around the world can spend time with their own one-of-a-kind companion in their own language.  The Mind Runs on Your PC  For the mind, AIvy is a local LLM runner built on llama.cpp. On first launch you pick from a dropdown an open-source language model that fits your language and download it once. From then on it runs  fully offline , with no account, no API key, and no internet connection required. Your conversations are never sent anywhere.  You are not limited to the models listed in the app, either. Any GGUF file—say, one you grabbed from Hugging Face—works as AIvy's mind: pick it in settings or drop it into the models folder. There is no size cap, so a large model will run if your RAM allows.  In short, AIvy is the same kind of local LLM client as LM Studio, Jan, or GPT4All—just dressed up in a VRM character UI instead of a chat panel. The first-run download catalog is restricted to permissive licenses (Apache 2.0 / MIT) so the models are safe to use in commercial and streaming contexts.  The voice is delivered by your OS's built-in TTS. For something more characterful, there is Piper TTS: AIvy downloads and sets up both Piper itself and its voices from the settings panel, so there is  nothing to install separately . Voices are available for every supported language, and you can preview one before downloading it. If you already have VOICEVOX, AivisSpeech, Sharevox, or VoiSona Talk, you can connect those to AIvy as well.  A Quiet Presence, Designed Not to Get in the Way  AIvy isn't built to be the assistant that keeps interrupting you—it's built to be the companion whose presence you simply feel. When you're focused, it watches over you in silence. In a quieter moment, it might softly check in with "Maybe time for a break?" or "Done with that video?"—a single line that fits the situation. And whenever you feel like talking, it's always there to answer. The mascot stays on top of every window but lets your clicks pass right through, so it never blocks your work. Every detail is tuned so it stays comfortable to have around, even on the longest workdays.  With these gentle gestures and the right kind of distance, AIvy adds a quiet color to your desktop life. In return, they’ll share elemental essences, a magic energy that will be of good use to bring the island back to life. short: Plan, build and ship with bossMAN, using your ChatGPT or Claude subscription or local AI models. The built-in Tracker helps turn large projects into manageable tasks to work through them step by step.
about: Crush your workload            A control room for AI-assisted development  bossMAN is a desktop workflow tool for Windows x64 and Apple Silicon Macs. Use ChatGPT through Codex, Claude or compatible local models to plan, build and manage your game-dev and software projects.   For game developers, bossMAN can help keep game projects, tooling repos, build notes, implementation plans, and review passes from turning into scattered one-off chat sessions.     Why bossMAN?     Highly customizable UI  for your AI-assisted projects to increase efficiency and tune aesthetics.     Assign avatars and voicepack audio playback  to your projects' activity to enhance multitasking and identity.     Tracker system  used to streamline and simplify longterm development of a project itemizing both scoped work and bugs items     Tracker workflows  help agents plan and work through selected tasks using your project settings. Permissions and approval behavior depend on the selected backend and configuration.     Manage local game-dev and software projects  locally and via SSH.      Included runtimes and AI access  The Steam purchase includes the bossMAN desktop application, Codex and Claude runtimes, and local inference runtimes. You do not need to install Codex CLI or Claude Code separately to use those backends on this computer.  You can open bossMAN and use built-in Help without a ChatGPT or Claude subscription. Hosted AI requires internet access and your own eligible ChatGPT or Claude subscription. Connect an existing account through the selected provider's sign-in flow. Subscriptions are obtained separately outside bossMAN; the Steam purchase includes no provider subscription or AI usage credits. Provider terms, availability and usage limits apply.  Local AI requires a compatible model file and suitable hardware. Local chat-model files are not included, and model licenses, memory and storage requirements vary. A hosted AI subscription is not required for local AI. Allow extra storage for models, projects and development tools. Downloads and connected tools may require internet access. name: Thirsty Snail Demo
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Unhinged snails have taken over your desktop. A growing collection of weirdos — they bicker, they roast you, they judge your life choices. Your typing keeps them alive. They are not grateful.
about: It's a normal day at your desk and there are snails everywhere.    A whole crowd of snails, each with its own personality and opinions. Strange species, fantasy designs, bizarre mutants, and combos that start arguing the moment they meet. Collect them for the album, watch them interact, or just let them do their thing while you work.     Snail Thirsty, Snail Foolish.      You Type, it rains.            Write code, grind out an essay, browse the internet. Every keystroke drops rain onto your screen, and that's how the snails stay hydrated.  Well-watered snails are energetic and active. Thirsty ones slow down and start looking for water. If they dry out completely, they retreat into their shells until your next typing session.     A Shell for Every Occasion           Samurai, ninja, pirate, vampire, wizard, scientist, mythical creature, strange mutant, and many more desktop residents waiting to be discovered.  Five rarity tiers. Unlock new snails through exploration, crafting, and idle rewards. The album is never truly full.     Hand-Drawn. Overdramatic.              Every snail has multiple individually drawn animation states. No simple recolors, no cheap reskins.  Happy ones bounce. Moody ones retreat into their shells. Small details like these are everywhere if you pay attention. Each one is worth watching on its own.     Can't shut up. Won't shut up.           Put two snails next to each other and they start talking. Some are polite, some pick fights. Different combos trigger completely different conversations.  They also react to your desktop interactions and may occasionally comment on them. Poke them too much and they get annoyed. Pick them up and they complain. Ignore them for too long, and they may come looking for trouble.  Even when nobody is paying attention, they keep themselves busy. They mutter to themselves, talk more at night, and may trigger hidden Easter eggs during special dates or random events. Special dates and random events hide extra content that you either stumble into or miss entirely.  Desktop interaction is designed around a local-first experience. The app does not read or upload the contents of your private files.     Grab. Drag. Drop.           Pick them up. Fling them around. Stick one to the side of the screen, and it will climb along the edge.  Drop one from too high and it panics into its shell. Let two favorites bump into each other and hearts show up.  Transparent background, sits at the bottom of your screen. Doesn't get in the way.       Race. Steal. Revenge.           Send one of your snails over to a friend's desktop.  Race them for water, or sneak in and skim some off the top. Your call.   Two snails, one screen, winner takes water.   Lost the race? Call for revenge. Caught mid-steal? Your snail slinks home with nothing. Travel Frog? Meet Thirsty Snail. Every race and every heist gets logged. Unclaimed water is one click away.     Features     Many unique snails across five rarity tiers, with multiple ways to unlock them.    Snails have multiple animation states. No simple recolors, no cheap reskins.    Your keystrokes power the ecosystem. More typing, more rain.    Put snails together and they start talking on their own.    Snails react to what's on your desktop. All processing happens locally.    AI conversations with memory. Snails can remember your interactions and respond with their own speaking styles.    Drag, toss, climb walls, fall from high places.    Send snails to friends' desktops. Race for water, pull off heists, claim rewards from the activity log.    Transparent background. Stays out of the way while you work.

name: Agent Guild: World
lang: English
short: A free, living 3D world for your AI coding agents. Every Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok and shell session you run with Agent Guild becomes a character at its guild hall. Make your own characters and companions in the in-app Studio and share them in the Imagination Station.
about: Every Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok and shell session you run with Agent Guild becomes a character at its guild hall, working while its agent works and resting when it goes quiet.    Agent Guild: World is free, and it sets itself up. On first launch it installs the free Agent Guild for you, Node.js included, with no administrator rights and no AI account needed to start. Then fly around six worlds, make your own characters, pin up your notes and earn achievements for the work you ship.    Make your own characters and companions  Bring a rigged humanoid model (.glb, .gltf, .vrm or .fbx) and the in-app Studio fits it to the world's skeleton, every animation intact. Make it a crew's character or a set of companions, or recolor one of the world's own looks, and preview it by day and at dusk.          Publish your pieces to the Imagination Station, World's Steam Workshop, from inside the app, or subscribe to other people's and choose them in Looks. The first pieces came out for Halloween: Patchwork Giants and Jack-o'-lanterns.            Your notes and to-dos, pinned up in the world  Every world has its own Guild Board. Your Agent Guild notes pin up as cards, ticked to-dos show as done, and the latest news hangs beside them. Open the board to write and edit; the notes are the same everywhere you use Agent Guild.            Six worlds you can fly around  Orbit, tilt and zoom anywhere with mouse, keyboard or controller, by day or at dusk. The Guild Yard, Orbital Station, The Living Grove, Operations Campus, Goblinville Works and Gnomeland Village each have their own halls and crews.            Achievements for real work  Twenty-one to earn. Six come from World, from opening for business to touring all six worlds. Fifteen come from the work itself: merged pull requests, passing workflow runs and closed issues, with three-tier ladders to climb and a Hat Trick for all three in one day (Agent Guild 1.6 or newer, signed in to GitHub).            Also in World    Open any session in a full terminal, then go back to the world.    Start a new session from its tool's hall.    Watch any computer running Agent Guild, added with a sign-in link.    Full controller support and a Steam Deck preset.    Light on your machine: it idles at 30 frames a second and stops drawing while hidden.      Works with the free Agent Guild  World runs on the free Agent Guild and sets it up for you, Node.js included, with no administrator rights. Your coding tools are installed and signed in through Agent Guild as usual.          Session management, usage meters and the GitHub panel stay in Agent Guild, on the web, in VS Code and on your other devices.

MythTunes is a featherweight desktop music player built for players — drop in your local folders and your whole collection becomes a pixel-perfect jukebox.   Add any folder from your computer and let the built-in Lofi & Vibe selection set the mood — focus, relaxation, or pure atmosphere. Add as many folders as you like; everything shows up in one place. 🎵 AUDIO PLAYBACK & LIBRARY  High-quality playback for a wide range of audio formats, in classic pixel style. Breathe Life with Your Keyboard and Mouse  Every keystroke and mouse click while you work or study becomes healing energy that brings stars back to life. Watch barren planets bloom into beautiful worlds.               A Tiny Ecosystem with Real-Time Day & Night  As the main planet rotates, warm sunlight and quiet night shadows shift across the mini-diorama in real time. Each time the Assistant plunges a giant syringe at the Doctor's cue, diverse ecosystems—from glowing spore mushroom forests to tropical archipelagos—bloom right before your eyes.               Customize Your Cozy Desktop Terrarium  Decorate your monitor with frame themes and healing effects unlocked each time you restore a planet. That’s the kind of desk you can build in Little Loops. Find your first favorite        Start with a popper, a spinner and 250 joy. Pick a bonsai, a pottery wheel or an aquarium as a welcome gift. There are 16 toys and activities to discover. Trim a branch, trail bubbles through the fish tank, flip a pancake or load a parcel onto the Pocket railway and send it to the orchard or the lakeside cottage. Try a toy in the Shop before you spend any joy on it. At the clockmaker’s bench        The observatory needs a slow sweep hand. Which wheels will get it there? Fit four gears, wind the movement and watch the dial. A six-second test records your reading. There are three orders to work through, each with its own limits on speed, direction or space. It’s the kind of game you open for  “just one quick match”  and somehow realize you’ve been rolling dice for the last thirty minutes.  At its core, it’s just  classic backgammon . No weird rule changes, no card systems, no unnecessary layers. But the presentation has a bit more punch: dice roll, checkers slam into place, hits feel satisfying, and big moments actually feel like big moments.  And when you feel like taking it seriously, there’s  Ranked .  Win, climb, lose, blame the dice, queue again, and work your way up the leaderboard. Backgammon is part strategy, part risk, and part convincing yourself that your opponent is unbelievably lucky.    Classic Backgammon   No classes, no deckbuilding, no seventeen different currencies. Move your checkers, hit your opponent, build your board and bear off first.   Built to Sit on the Side   No need to dedicate your whole screen to it. Keep the game in a small window while you watch, work, browse or do anything else.              “Just One Quick Game”   Matches are fast. Launching the game shouldn’t feel like a commitment — it’s there to turn a spare couple of minutes into a match.   Way More Satisfying Than It Needs to Be   Dice rolls, checker movement, hits and key moments are brought to life with snappy animations and effects.             Ranked & Leaderboards   Casual games not enough? Queue up, climb your rating and see how competitive a tiny backgammon window can get.   Small window. Quick matches. Big backgammon ego.

about: Someone left a glass jar on your desk. Inside is a tiny island: a hill of grass, a sandy beach, a lake full of fish and a little village with its torches burning. It’s yours now. Dig into it. Flood it. Pour lava down the hill and watch the lake boil. Or leave it be and watch the world go on without you. There are no goals, no score and no wrong way to play. Just a small living world that sits on your desktop while you work.   Features      Shape the land with your hands.  Pour sand, soil and stone wherever you like. Carve valleys, raise mountains, dig caves. Every grain falls, piles up and slides like the real thing.     Water that finds its own way.  Pour it from the watering can and it pools, spills and runs downhill. A running stream slowly cuts its own path through the hills, and rivers change course over time.     Play with fire and lava.  Lava glows, flows and crusts over as it cools into new rock. When it reaches the water, it hisses and steams. Grass catches fire, and rain puts it out.     A world that’s alive.  Fish scatter when your hand comes near. Trees sway in the breeze. Butterflies drift by in the day and fireflies come out at night. Torches flicker in the dark and go out when they get wet.     Become a villager or any other critter.  You can take over any living creatures and play from first or third person as any critter!     Build your own village.  Place houses, torches, trees and rocks. Build with blocks. Make a quiet fishing village or a castle on a cliff.     It lives on your desktop.  The jar sits on top of your other windows, and clicks outside it pass right through to whatever you’re doing. Drag it anywhere, make it bigger or smaller, and check in on it whenever you like.     Never lose a thing.  Everything saves by itself. Close the game and come back tomorrow. Your world will be right where you left it.

name: Taskbar Legends
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Portuguese - Portugal, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: An online idle auto-battler that lives on your taskbar. Build your party, upgrade and ascend heroes, collect tradable loot and push deeper into endless expeditions and dungeons.
about: Taskbar Legends is an online idle auto-battler for Windows that lives right on your taskbar. Build your party, manage gear, craft, summon new heroes and choose where to explore. Then get back to work while your heroes keep fighting, earning loot and progressing in the background. Open the hub whenever you want to check your progress or prepare for the next expedition.         Choose six heroes and position them across three rows: Front, Mid and Back. Where you place each hero matters. Tanks are built to hold the front line, melee fighters thrive in the middle, while healers, ranged heroes and support characters work best from behind.     Front:  Tanks absorb damage and hold the line.     Mid:  Melee heroes deal damage from the heart of the fight.     Back:  Healers, ranged heroes and support keep the party alive from a safer position.    Every hero has a unique kit, and each brings different damage schools to the fight. Bosses can resist or be vulnerable to certain schools, so the team that clears one map may not be the right team for the next. Experiment with your lineup and formation to find the best combination for every encounter.         Every hero you summon has its own level and tier. Take them into battle to gain permanent levels, equip them with loot, or collect three matching heroes of the same tier and bring them to the Ascension Forge.     Level:  Heroes gain permanent power as they fight.     Gear:  Strengthen your party with loot, crafting and gems.     Ascend:  Fuse three matching heroes into one hero of the next tier, up to Tier 5.    The Forge carries over the average level of the three heroes you combine. Three Level 50 heroes become a single higher-tier Level 50 hero, with a new appearance on the battlefield and additional stars on your roster.         Tradable heroes and eligible gear are stored as Steam Inventory items. When you add a hero to your party or equip an item, it becomes locked to your account until you remove it. Your active heroes and gear can never be traded while they're in use.     Protected loadouts:  Heroes in your party and equipped gear cannot be traded.     Clear upgrades:  Upgrading an item exchanges it for a new item rather than silently changing the original.     A living economy:  Heroes and eligible gear can be traded, while packs, materials, food and energy items remain outside the market.           Send your party into an expedition for a single run or keep pushing through an endless session. Every completed run permanently secures its gold, XP and loot, so the further you go, the more you can bring home.     Complete a run:  Your rewards are secured immediately and the next lap begins with stronger enemies.     Retreat:  Keep everything you've already secured, but lose the rewards from your current run.     Lose:  Previously secured rewards, your heroes and their equipped gear are always safe.    Return to camp to recover, restore energy and prepare food for your next expedition. Food buffs run in real time, so prepare your supplies before you set out.         Taskbar Legends is online-only, with your account, inventory, rewards and progression securely managed on the server. Combat is also server-authoritative, keeping rewards and progression fair and preventing local files from being used to fake clears or generate loot.     Live hub:  See who's online and chat with other players.     Daily and weekly activities:  Earn rewards through daily login rewards, daily quests and weekly quests.     Adventures and activities:  Explore, return to camp, craft, cook and fish.     Codex:  Track heroes, enemies, items, builds and your overall progression.    Designed to Stay Out of Your Way  The taskbar overlay is click-through and won't steal focus from whatever you're doing. Hide it when you want a clean desktop, then bring it back whenever you're ready to check your heroes or plan your next expedition.     An internet connection and Steam sign-in are required.

about: Taskbar Kingdom is a medieval idle game that lives along the bottom of your desktop. Your castle, your villagers and your army sit right above the taskbar — while you write, code, browse or watch, your realm keeps growing on its own.  Everything outside the game passes straight through: clicks go to your desktop, your windows stay usable, and the kingdom is there whenever you glance down.           The Crown has entrusted you with a small, forgotten castle on the frontier. Send villagers to the fields, the forest and the mine. Gather resources, upgrade your buildings and raise your castle, level by level.           Raiders come at intervals — swordsmen, axemen, archers, crossbowmen, and catapults that target your walls. Train swordsmen, spearmen, archers, crossbowmen and knights, then build watchtowers and stretch walls between them. Battles play out on their own, right on your screen.  Lose a fight and you're plundered, but you never start from zero. Repair, regroup and come back stronger.           Once your castle stands firm, take the fight to them. Send troops on expeditions that last from minutes to hours in real time. Every expedition is a real choice: while your soldiers are away, your castle is weaker.           Expeditions lead across a hand-crafted map of regions, each with its own reward. Every region you take is yours to keep. Earn renown and climb the ranks: Marcher Lord, Knight, Count, Marquis, Duke and, at last, Hand of the Crown.              Lives on your desktop  borderless, transparent and always on top, with clicks passing through to your desktop.       Three kingdoms to serve  each with its own strengths and trade-offs. None is simply "the best".     Five unit types , watchtowers, walls and real-time raids.     Loot and chest  items across six rarities, from Common to Mythic. Merge duplicates into stronger gear.     Skill tree  with three branches, earned only by playing.     Quests  that guide you without holding your hand.     Resize and move  the scene to fit your screen.     No pay-to-win . Ever.

about: Grimoire Garden: A Taskbar Tale   is a cozy, second-screen taskbar game that perfectly blends idle farming, satisfying progression, and fast-paced typing combat. Designed to live comfortably at the bottom of your screen, it turns your desktop into a living magical sanctuary. Whether you are working, studying, or watching a stream, your garden grows alongside you without ever interrupting your workflow.  Join your loyal magic apprentice, Pip, and your feathered friend, Sparrow Jack Junior, to cultivate enchanted crops, fend off greedy goblins, and build the ultimate magical treasury!    🌱  Farming on the Edge of Your Screen    Start with a single taskbar planter and invest your hard-earned gold to expand your garden. Plant magical seeds, watch them progress through 4 growth stages, and harvest them for profit. The game is fully aware of your desktop environment. It scales dynamically, detects when your taskbar is set to auto-hide (smoothly sliding up and down with it), and lets you choose exactly which monitor your garden blooms on.          ⏳  Meaningful Offline Progress & Upgrades    Your garden respects your time. Invest gold and harvested crops into a deep skill tree to unlock permanent, powerful buffs. Contributed crops cannot be sold, but they grant massive improvements like the Market License (+25% Sell Value), Double Pack (25% chance for double harvests), or Turbo Roots (+80% Growth Speed). Need to close the game? Unlock the Scarecrow for offline growth, or reach the ultimate Dance Powder upgrade so your plants grow and water themselves entirely while your PC is turned off!     ⚔️  Seamless "No-Spacebar" Typing Combat    Goblins will try to steal your crops! Defeat them using our seamless Typing Combat. Just type the magical words above their heads to instantly cast spells (no spacebar needed!).    Find Grimoires: Unlock higher difficulty levels to face tougher goblins with significantly better loot drop chances.    The Skeleton Minigame: Trigger an epic boss fight! Deflect the Skeleton's magical bone projectile back and forth up to 20 times. Based on your skill, you will earn "Bone Meal" (Tier 1 to 20). This is a powerful Fever Mode item that massively accelerates your garden's growth.             📅  Daily Quests & The Bonus Stash    Keep things fresh with 3 Daily Quests (you can reroll up to 3 times a day). Completing quests rewards you with temporary, powerful perks like Caffeine Rush (+150% growth speed for 2 hours) or Auto-Watering. These perks are stored in your 9-slot "Bonus Stash". Drag and drop them to activate them whenever you need a boost. Complete all 3 daily quests to earn a guaranteed max-level Tier 20 Bone Meal!      🐦  Jack Jr.: From Egg to Legendary Companion    Before Sparrow Jack Junior becomes your loyal companion, you need to help him hatch! It all begins with a mysterious egg sitting on the edge of your screen. Every global keystroke and mouse click you make outside the game (while working or chatting) helps crack the shell. Once hatched, your continued activity levels him up. After every ascension, his XP resets, but his loot pool expands! Level him up to max level (11) so he can drop the rarest, most valuable seeds, including the legendary Sunflower.    🎡  Skill-Based Wheel of Fortune    Feeling lucky? Use a free spin or earn Wheel Tokens from daily quests to spin the Wheel of Fortune. Time it perfectly with your own skill to reliably snag the exact rare seed you need for your next big upgrade!    📊  Stats, Achievements & Completionism     Love numbers? Grimoire Garden tracks everything: total global keystrokes, mouse clicks, gold earned, specific goblin types defeated, and exact crop yields.    59 Steam Achievements: Challenge yourself to unlock them all! From your very first sprout to the ultimate Platinum Achievement, there is a rewarding milestone for every stage of your journey. Flex your efficiency and watch your numbers go up while you work.

about: About the Demo   This demo offers a taste of living with cats and decorating your room.  The selection of cats, furniture, rooms, music, gameplay features, and other content is limited compared with the full game.          Neko Room Days  is a cozy 2D pixel-art room-decorating sim where you create a home for cats and unwind to mellow lo-fi music.  Care for your cats, arrange furniture, or use the music and built-in timers while you work. Whatever you are in the mood for, spend your time in the cat room your own way.                A Home Full of Little Cat Moments  Your cats roam freely around the room, eating, drinking, playing, and curling up in their favorite spots. Pet and brush them, get to know each cat on their own terms, and watch friendships grow as they spend time together.                                Make the Cat Room Your Own  Your life together begins in a compact studio apartment. Collect and arrange more than 20 types of furniture, including cat beds, towers, tunnels, toys, and a cozy kotatsu.  As your level rises, new places to live become available, including a traditional Japanese room, a high-rise apartment, and a resort villa. Each of the six rooms takes on a different atmosphere in the morning, afternoon, and at night.                       Lo-Fi for Focus and Relaxation  Choose from six albums featuring 60+ lo-fi tracks. Skip to the next track, shuffle playback, or turn on repeat.  The Pomodoro timer and stopwatch run independently of the music and can be used at the same time. Let the cats and music keep you company while you work, study, or read.                             Everyday Moments Become Memories  Your first time caring for a cat, the changing atmosphere from morning to night, discovering new rooms and furniture, and seeing two cats grow closer—these moments can all be recorded as Memories as you reach milestones throughout the game.  Let your cats take on part-time jobs and wait for them to come home, or hide the UI and simply enjoy the room and music. There is no need to rush. Spend time with your cats and make memories at your own pace.            A little company on your taskbar while you work   Switch to Mini Mode and let your cats step out of their room and onto your desktop. Watch them stroll along your taskbar or curl up for a peaceful nap. Whether you’re working or studying, they’ll quietly keep you company.  Put on your favorite lo-fi music and make your everyday tasks a little cozier, with cats by your side.

name: Butterflies & Bloom
lang: English
short: A cottagecore typing companion. A transparent flower garden lives just above your taskbar and blooms as you write, code, and chat. Sell flowers for coins, attract bees and butterflies, build a garden out of the hours you already spend at the keyboard.
about: Butterflies & Bloom is a quiet typing companion that lives above your taskbar. A row of flowers grows there, one seed per slot, blooming a little more with every keystroke. There is no full-screen world to enter, no level to start. The garden is simply there, alongside everything else you're doing — writing, coding, replying to emails, working on a thesis — turning the hours you'd spend typing anyway into something soft and cumulative.  How It Works  Open the Shop, buy a seed for a few coins, plant it. Every key you press nudges that flower's growth meter forward. When it fully blooms, sell it back for twice what the seed cost — and use the profit to buy rarer, prettier, more expensive seeds. Rinse and repeat at your own pace. Whether you're a hunt-and-peck typist or hammering out a hundred words a minute, the garden keeps up with you.  The Garden Loop      Buy seeds with coins      Plant your garden      Type — the more you type, the more they bloom      Sell bloomed flowers for a profit      Repeat    Bees, Butterflies, Dragonflies, Ladybugs  Four kinds of garden visitors drift through, each with a different gameplay effect: bees nudge growth forward without you typing, butterflies multiply your sell value, dragonflies make every keystroke worth more coins, and ladybugs slowly drip passive income. Each comes in five rarity tiers (Common through Legendary) with distinct color palettes — and every visitor is animated procedurally, so no two are exactly alike.  720+ Flowers to Discover  Twelve archetypes × six rarities × ten color palettes = 720 unique flowers. Rarer flowers take more keystrokes to bloom but sell for far more. The shop rotates every eight hours; the Mythic-tier flowers cost a small fortune and reward a small fortune. Patience is part of the loop.  Privacy is the Whole Point  The game needs system permission to count your keystrokes — and that's all it does. Every key you press advances the counter by one. Which key you pressed is never read, stored, logged, transmitted, or used in any way. We don't capture text. We don't read mouse content. The keystroke counter never leaves your machine.   Petals (Optional)  For those who want to skip ahead, "Petals" is an optional real-money currency that buys instant insects and seed packs. The entire core loop — every flower, every visitor, every tier — is reachable by typing alone. Petals are convenience, never required.  Designed to Disappear  The overlay is transparent and click-through. It never steals focus, never makes a sound, never pings you. When you bring your mouse near the flowers they politely fade out so you can use the dock or taskbar underneath. Open the Shop or Garden tabs when you want to play with the loop; ignore the whole thing on a deadline and your flowers will still be there when you're done.

name: The Flattening
lang: English
short: Explore a colorful open world inside an early-2000s operating system, meet its living programs and characters, race, explore, and fight back as a mysterious update slowly transforms their utopian world into something flat, corporate, and lifeless. Your actions determine how the story ends.
about: Every morning, the world assembles.    You live inside an operating system. Not a metaphor for one — an actual, utopian, 2000s  operating system, where every part of the world is a living character.    When the computer user hits the power button, everyone takes their place. The taskbar straightens  up. The folders line up. The icons hold still and look like icons. The user gets a  seamless desktop and never finds out how much work that was.    When the computer goes off, everyone clocks out and goes to hang around.       You're the mascot for a messaging app. You know everybody, everybody likes you, and  somehow that's made you a sort of leader — not officially. Just the one who ends up in  charge.    Realms    Your world is many worlds, connected. Each one is built out of a design theme that  everybody loved back then — glass and water, green hills and blue sky, gloss and bubbles  and optimism. You love this place more than you say out loud.         Then you and Bob went too far.    It started as a race. You and your best friend, out past the parts of the world you know.    That's where you saw it.         The color is being taken out. Whole regions of it, flattened and squared off and drained  grey. It's an update — one that's stripping every whimsical, glossy, over-designed thing  your world is made of and replacing it with corporate flat design.    It is not slowing down.    So you and your friends are going to stop it. With everything you have.

about: ■ This is  not  an idle game.   Hunk & Doggo  is a desktop companion app where two quiet souls live their peaceful lives in the corner of your screen. It’s not about efficiency or automation.  Instead, it offers a calm, gentle presence. Just keep it running — and their quiet days will unfold on their own.          ■ Hunk — A quiet, clumsy middle-aged miner  He doesn’t say much, but he keeps mining steadily. He seems content with his quiet life alongside Doggo.            ■ Doggo — A carefree and curious companion  He mimics Hunk’s digging, gets soaked when it rains, and runs around the screen doing whatever he likes. He lives freely — just being himself.  ■ An app where you don’t  need  to do anything  Even as the level rises, your role doesn’t change. You  can  interact — collect falling grass, pop a balloon — but you don’t have to.  Sometimes the keyboard triggers something, sometimes it rains. These small changes are subtle and satisfying.  ■ Includes a simple Pomodoro timer  A built-in  Pomodoro timer  helps you manage focus and rest. While you work, Hunk and Doggo quietly keep you company.  ■ Doesn’t get in the way — but you might want it always on  It’s designed to stay out of your way, but you may find yourself wanting it there all the time.  Just above the taskbar, in the corner of your screen — a peaceful companion for your desktop.

name: Note&Pad
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Polish, Thai, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Vietnamese, Korean
short: A desktop text editor with sticky notes. Opens hundreds of megabytes in seconds and keeps memory flat no matter the file size. Unsaved changes are snapshotted automatically, so a crash costs you nothing. 22 encodings, 15 interface languages, and every theme and string editable.
about: Large files stay cheap Files hundreds of megabytes in size open within seconds. Viewer mode and windowed editing decouple memory usage from file size, so even a huge log won't drag down the whole machine. Jump to line and streaming search work on files of any size. Sticky notes on the desktop One shortcut opens a note; it saves as you type. Pin it above everything, have it follow a specific app, or just use it as a normal window. Opacity is adjustable, and any note is one click away from the Dock menu or the taskbar jump list. A real editor underneath    Syntax highlighting, detected automatically or set by hand    Find and replace, one at a time or all at once    Line endings (LF/CRLF) and encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16, Big5, Shift_JIS, 22 in total) switch on the fly    Word wrap and line numbers toggle independently    Full menu bar and shortcuts that follow each platform's conventions   Nothing gets lost Unsaved changes are snapshotted automatically. If the app closes unexpectedly, the content is still there when you reopen it. Closing a window with unsaved changes always asks first. A file with more than roughly 16 million characters of unsaved changes is too large to snapshot, so the app won't quit until you save or discard it. Nothing gets lost that way. Make it yours 10 built-in themes, editable in place or saved as your own. Themes are plain data files: export to share, import from others, restore in one click. 15 interface languages, and every line of interface text can be rewritten and saved as a language file of your own. Works entirely offline No account, no telemetry, nothing sent anywhere.

name: MysteryOS - AXIOM/2
lang: English
short: A corporate alien OS hides a collective intelligence across three desktops. 60 standalone puzzle apps. 87 achievements. Compliance is mandatory. The Foundation is watching. The Resonance is rising.
about: The signal from AXIOM/1 didn't go unnoticed.  You've been pulled into NexusOS, a corporate desktop interface built by the Kron'thul network. It looks almost familiar: file browsers, text editors, system monitors. But nothing works the way you expect. The language is alien. The compliance system tracks your every action. And somewhere behind the corporate facade, something ancient is watching.   What lurks beneath the surface?   Navigate a fully interactive alien operating system across three desktops — corporate Workspace, hidden Commons, and the Foundation that bleeds through when the Kron'thul aren't looking. Solve interconnected puzzles. Build compliance. Obey the system. Or don't. The network remembers everything, and the taskbar holds more secrets than you think.   What's in AXIOM/2:       20 interconnected story puzzles with a branching dependency graph    60 standalone bonus apps across three desktops, each with its own self-contained alien mechanic    Three variants per bonus app — Primary (the canonical experience), Light (a quick single-trick puzzle), and Weird (the ambitious, screenshot-worthy version)    87 Steam achievements to hunt, including legendary unlocks for the Weird variants    The Resonance system: a hidden parallel score that tracks how the Foundation perceives you    Pipe routing, compliance management, base-7 arithmetic, glyph decipherment, and social engineering challenges    Real consequences for wrong actions: system crashes, lockouts, and data loss    Multiple danger zones with colorblind-safe non-linguistic warning cues    Five to eight hours of core gameplay, plus dozens more for full achievement completion     Requires the free base game (MysteryOS) and is best played with AXIOM/1 completed.

name: "Did You Submit a Ticket?" Simulator
lang: English**
short: Welcome to your new job. HelpDesk OS is a corporate IT support simulator where you battle frustrated coworkers using logic, dialogue, and weaponized company policy. Drain their willpower, manage their rage, and survive your 9-to-5 shift without HR firing you. Have you tried turning it off and on?
about: Congratulations on your new role as a Level 1 IT Support Technician!  Clock in, sit down, and log into  HelpDesk OS , a fully simulated corporate operating system where your only weapon against the endless tide of broken printers, forgotten passwords, and screaming executives is your keyboard.  In this narrative-driven simulation puzzle game, every support ticket is a boss fight. You must navigate complex dialogue trees to resolve issues while managing the delicate balance of your coworkers'  Willpower  and  Rage .   A Fully Simulated OS   Navigate a nostalgic, fully interactive desktop environment. Drag windows, minimize tabs to your taskbar, and juggle multiple applications at once. Use the Employee Directory to look up caller details, open the Messenger to handle tickets, and keep an eye on the clock. You just have to survive until 5:00 PM.   Combat via Chat (Willpower vs. Rage)   This isn't just customer service; it's tactical combat. Every coworker has a Willpower meter (their resistance to following your instructions) and a Rage meter (their frustration level).     Drain their Willpower:  Pick the right dialogue options to break down their stubbornness until they finally submit a ticket.     Manage their Rage:  Be careful—if you are too blunt or unhelpful, their Rage will spike. If an employee's Rage hits 100%, you get escalated to HR and you're fired.     Weaponize the SLA Rulebook   When logic fails, bureaucracy prevails. Open your company's SLA (Service Level Agreement) Rulebook to look up exact corporate policies. Cite the correct rule to instantly shut down unreasonable demands and deal massive damage to an employee's Willpower.   Key Features:      Dynamic Dialogue Trees:  Every employee has different starting stats and requires different tactics to defeat.     Immersive Desktop Metaphor:  A complete, interactive UI that feels like a real computer desktop.     A Cast of Corporate Nightmares:  Face off against Dave from Accounting, Sarah from HR, and the terrifying VP of Marketing who refuses to listen to reason.     Real-time Typing Mechanics:  Experience the agonizing suspense of watching the "Employee is typing..." indicator.     Geared Games Studios reminds you: Time theft is a fireable offense. Get back to work.

Stress Relief Gadget for 'Workers':   We understand the need to find a moment of peace amid complex work. name: CEO.exe
lang: English, German
short: An idle game about becoming CEO, played entirely on a simulated 1990s office PC. File paperwork by hand, automate it away, hire the staff who replace you — then scheme your way through the boardroom. Every mechanic is a program on the desktop.
about: Nobody becomes CEO by working hard. They become CEO by arranging for the work to happen without them.    CEO.exe is an idle game about climbing a corporate ladder, played entirely inside a simulated 1990s office computer — a machine that boots, hums, glows and occasionally crashes. No HUD, no menu screen. A desktop, a taskbar, and a slowly growing number of programs you had to earn.  File it yourself. Then never again.  You start by dragging documents into the filer one at a time, paid per document, binning the red carbons before they cost you the work. Then you write the batch files that do it for you, requisition better hardware out of the IT budget, and set the TURBO jumper to run the machine past what it is rated for. It will get you through the afternoon. It will also, eventually, hand you a blue screen.  Hire the people who replace you  Manager grade gets you staff. Your section clears the tray while you do something else — as long as morale holds, wages go out at 17:00, and you notice who is drowning. The loop you spent an hour mastering becomes a line item somebody else handles.  Then it stops being about the work  At Director there is a table, six rivals and not enough chairs. Influence buys schemes: take credit for somebody else's quarter, strike an alliance, quietly undermine the man ahead of you. Every reorganisation removes the weakest director in the room. Sometimes that is you.  It runs while you are gone  Close the game and the section keeps working. Come back to a payslip, a full inbox and whatever resolved without you. A full climb from intern to the top floor runs roughly nine to ten hours, built to be played in the gaps of a day.       A whole fake OS: draggable windows, a boot sequence, error dialogs, and a curved CRT you can turn the scanlines down on    SNAKE.EXE and MINES.EXE, for when the tray can wait     A run timer and achievements for a second, faster climb       No microtransactions, no ads, no timer that asks you for money      CEO.exe is in active development. Follow and Wishlist to stay updated on the process and be the first to play the upcoming Demo!

How to Play   Step into the role of a detective investigating the murder of a notorious crime boss. Search a sprawling forest and a decrepit warehouse for scattered evidence—including the victim’s body parts. Once you’ve found everything, escape back to the station before it’s too late.    But be warned:  Your microphone is your enemy. Make a sound, and you might not survive.      Features      Microphone Detection  Speak or make noise, and the game reacts.
