name: Desktop Gremlins
lang: English, Russian, Ukrainian, Japanese, Italian, Polish
short: A transparent desktop pet with five character forms, Chaos Mode, Steam Workshop, window attachment, Twitch integration, and online multiplayer. Feed and pet your gremlin, let viewers trigger pranks live, or invite a friend through Steam to join the chaos
about: MEET THE LITTLE MENACE LIVING ON YOUR DESKTOP   Desktop Gremlins  is a living desktop companion that stays right on your screen. It wanders between your windows, reacts to music and the applications you open, asks for attention, gets tired, falls asleep-and definitely notices when you forget to feed it.  Give your gremlin a name, feed it, pet it, pick it up or offer it a cup of coffee. You can also choose exactly where it is allowed to walk, so it stays out of the way while you work, draw, study, play or stream.    CARE FOR IT. WATCH IT EVOLVE.  Your companion has hunger, affection, energy and experience. Everyday interactions help it grow from a tiny slime through  five distinct forms , each with its own appearance, animations, reactions and personality.       Feed, pet, grab and play with your companion       Watch it react to music and popular applications      Rename it and define a custom invisible walking zone       Control actions with global hotkeys, mouse buttons, gamepads and macro devices       Discover new moods, animations and dialogue as it changes      LET YOUR VIEWERS JOIN THE CHAOS  Connect Twitch and turn Channel Points into real interactions on your stream. Viewers can feed or pet the gremlin, give it coffee, send on-screen messages, trigger character reactions or unleash visual effects.  You remain in control: select up to  25 rewards , set their prices, adjust effect duration and customize alerts. Redemptions enter a queue instead of activating all at once, keeping busy streams entertaining without turning them into a slideshow.    Custom alerts with viewer names, avatars and emotes      Moderated on-screen messages with unsafe words automatically masked       Streamer Mode for hiding private account and connection information       OBS Browser Source support for effects above full-screen Game Capture      Every reward and notification can be enabled or disabled separately        CHAOS—ONLY WHEN YOU ALLOW IT  Enable Chaos Mode and your gremlin may shake or move windows, play with the cursor, flash the taskbar and launch harmless desktop pranks. It can be mischievous, but  it never closes your applications , and every disruptive feature is optional.  Prefer a peaceful companion? Leave Chaos Mode disabled. The gremlin will still live on your desktop, react to what you do and keep you company without rearranging your day.  MAKE YOUR GREMLIN YOURS  Subscribe to community-made sprite packs through  Steam Workshop , or use the built-in validation and upload tools to publish a complete character pack of your own.      Transparent, always-on-top desktop companion       Five evolving forms with unique animations and personalities      Needs, moods, stamina, sleep and experience systems      Reactions to music and the applications you use      Twitch Channel Points integration and customizable stream alerts      Optional Chaos Mode with configurable desktop pranks       Custom walking zones and flexible global controls      Steam Workshop support for community sprite packs       English, Ukrainian, Russian, Japanese, Polish and Italian      YOUR DESKTOP. YOUR GREMLIN. YOUR RULES.  It only wants a little food, a little affection-and perhaps complete control of your desktop. What could possibly go wrong?

name: WinHack 95
lang: English, German, Japanese, Simplified Chinese
short: Build a malware empire from a 90s PC. Code viruses, automate systems, take darknet contracts and also deploy them. Generate endless income to fund a shadow organization’s classified research in this hacker idle-clicker.
about: Build a malware empire from a single 90s PC.   You start with just a dusty machine.  You are working for a secret organization that needs you to earn money for their research.  Dont ask questions.               Turn code into money. Scale it endlessly.   Write viruses and deploy them.  Every operation generates income. Every upgrade multiplies it.  Start small — then build systems that run on their own.               Design, deploy, and automate your operation   Create malicious tools and automate them later on.  Turn active work into passive income. Turn small scripts into unstoppable infrastructure.               Shape your strategy   Build your operation through a deep upgrade system with 50+ nodes.  Focus on steady idle growth or high-risk high-reward plays.  Every choice changes how your system evolves.     Take contracts from the darknet   Accept illegal jobs and deliver the outcome under pressure.  The bigger the contract, the higher the risk.  Miss deadlines or attract attention and it might cost you everything.               Keep your system alive   Your machine is not safe. Not a single second.  Many different viruses can infect your system.  Identify the infections and take control again before everything collapses.               Dig deeper   Hidden inside the system are classified files maybe,  fragments of something bigger.  The more you grow, the more you uncover.  But some things were never meant to be found.     Features      A fully simulated Win95 desktop  - draggable windows, taskbar, persistent layout, and full CRT effects     Boot sequence and system lifecycle  - from BIOS-style startup to shutdown saves     Active + idle gameplay loops  - code manually or let your systems run automatically     Darknet contract system  - multiple tiers of illegal jobs with scaling rewards     Risk and failure mechanics  - police chases, system wipes, and permanent consequences     Deep progression system  - 50+ upgrades across multiple playstyles     Hidden dossiers and secrets  - discover classified data and piece together the truth     Dynamic events  - phishing, messages, and unexpected outcomes     System infections  - each virus changes how your machine behaves     Economic pressure  - rent, electricity, and costs keep increasing     Original soundtrack  - with lo-fi / hi-fi toggle inspired by 90s hardware     CRT simulation  - scanlines, flicker, and reactive visual effects     3 save slots  - with autosave and manual control      Do your daily job to finance the science  You wake up. You boot the machine.  You generate the money they need.  You do not ask questions.  If you are good — if you are very good — one day, the system might start answering back.

name: Shadow Realms RPG
lang: English
short: A free dark-fantasy idle RPG that keeps fighting in a strip above your taskbar while you work. One persistent world on Steam, web and Android with a single account: loot, world bosses, the endless Eternal, clan wars. No energy walls. Power is never for sale.
about: MINI MODE: AN RPG THAT FITS ABOVE YOUR TASKBAR Shrink Shadow Realms to a strip the size of a chat bar and keep working. Your hero keeps brawling: crits pop, bosses approach, Godforged drops flash, the kill counter and XP bar climb, and a Continue button waits when the run ends. Strike the World Boss straight from the strip. Expand to the full game whenever you want to spend what you earned. ONE HERO, THREE SCREENS The same account plays on Steam, in any browser and on Android. Farm in Mini Mode on your PC, check your loot on your phone at lunch, finish a dungeon on the web at night.  Forge your legend in Shadow Realms — a free dark-fantasy idle RPG you can play in seconds and keep for months.  Pick one of six classes, auto-battle through a haunted world of 19 zones, and grow from a lone adventurer into the terror of the realm. Your hero keeps fighting while you're away — every time you return there's loot to claim and levels to spend. ONE WORLD, EVERY PLATFORM No servers to pick and no realms that split you from your friends. Every player shares one persistent world: one economy, one leaderboard, one set of world bosses the whole realm hunts together. Play on Steam, the web, or Android with a single account and the same character everywhere. Your rank means something, because everyone is on the same ladder. ENDLESS AUTO-BATTLE Your hero fights on its own — offline too. Come back to gold, gear and XP, then take manual control for boss fights and ability rotations when you want the challenge. No energy timers, no waiting walls. ELEVEN COLOSSAL WORLD BOSSES Server-wide raid bosses the whole realm hunts together on a rotating schedule. Strike alongside everyone online, break them through phases, and claim loot scaled to the damage you deal — including unique Godforged relics. THE ENDLESS ETERNAL An infinite wave-survival gauntlet that scales forever. Climb for account-wide Ascension Shards, spend them on a prestige tree, and carve your name into the permanent global leaderboard. CLANS, CASTLES & WAR Found a clan, then build its fortress: upgrade castle stations, grow your roster, and raise a Clan Champion who defends the walls when rival realms invade. Push your clan's shared Eternal climb, run co-op clan dungeons, and fight weekly clan wars for the leaderboard crown. COMPANIONS TO RAISE & BREED Collect a growing stable of companions from bosses, dungeons, raids and limited-time events. Equip one for a real combat bonus, level it in battle, and breed two raised companions into rarer hybrids — all the way to a Primal-tier apex. HONEST PvP ARENA Challenge real players' builds in server-simulated duels. Defense is real effective-HP and every class has a signature — fights are fights, not coin-flips. Climb from Bronze to Immortal across monthly seasons. SEASONS & LIVE EVENTS Fresh-start Seasons open a level playing field — climb the seasonal ladder, earn Mastery, and graduate your champion. A new themed Battle Pass drops every month: 30 tiers on a fully free track, with season-exclusive cosmetics that never return. FAIR & GENEROUS The whole game is playable free — every boss, every rank, and all 30 Battle Pass tiers on the free track. Optional supporter cosmetics and convenience fund development. No content is locked behind a paywall. Power is never for sale.  Built and updated daily by one developer. The realm grows while you sleep.

name: Shoji Flow
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Arabic, Czech, Dutch, Hungarian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Swedish, Thai, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese
short: An intelligent window manager for Windows that learns how you work. Save your window setups as layouts and restore them with one click or a hotkey — Shoji Flow moves your windows into place, launches missing apps and suggests new layouts from your routines.
about: Stop dragging the same windows to the same spots every day. Shoji Flow saves the way you arrange your apps as layouts and brings them back with one click or a hotkey, across your monitors. It learns which setups you keep returning to and suggests new layouts on its own. Named after the sliding paper doors of Japanese architecture, it's built to feel calm and stay out of your way. Set up once. Back with one key. Capture your current window arrangement in one click, or build a layout by hand in the editor. Restoring a layout moves and resizes your windows back into place and launches the apps that aren't running yet, including Store and Electron apps. When you apply a layout from the app, a preview shows what will move and what will launch first, and if you change your mind, Undo puts your windows back where they were. For quick tidying in between, snap windows into halves, quarters or the center right from the dashboard.        It learns how you work Shoji Flow notices which apps you use together and how you arrange them: your morning coding setup, your streaming desk, your writing corner. Once a routine is clear, it suggests a ready-made layout, and one click opens it in the editor, ready to save. You decide how eager the suggestions are: Sensitive, Balanced or Strict. One hotkey, whole workspace Give any layout a global hotkey and switch your whole workspace from anywhere. Let Shoji Flow apply a layout the moment it starts, launch the apps a layout needs, and reopen a set of pages in your browser as fresh tabs.        Made for multiple monitors Per-monitor DPI scaling, and layouts that remember which screen each window belongs to. When your setup changes, windows land on the screens you have, inside the visible work area and never behind the taskbar. Rules per app Give an app its own color and display name, and decide how Shoji Flow treats it: skip it entirely (handy for games with anti-cheat), move it without resizing, or leave it alone in the tray. Noisy background apps can be hidden from Insights. Insights See how you really use your PC: your most-used apps, the combinations you run together, screen usage, active time per day and an hour-by-weekday heatmap. Optional AI Switch on the built-in AI and your layouts and suggestions get names, tags and short descriptions. It needs a one-time download of the AI model. Off by default. Share on the Steam Workshop Share your favorite layouts and import setups from other users. Plus Steam achievements to unlock along the way. And more   Back up all your layouts and settings into a single file and restore them anytime   Available in 21 languages

name: Big Sister
lang: English*, French*, Italian*, German*, Spanish - Spain*, Danish*, Ukrainian*, Russian*, Bulgarian*, Hungarian*, Indonesian*, Turkish*, Greek*, Norwegian*, Czech*, Japanese*, Polish*, Thai*, Swedish*, Simplified Chinese*, Traditional Chinese*, Romanian*, Finnish*, Dutch*, Portuguese - Brazil*, Portuguese - Portugal*, Spanish - Latin America*, Vietnamese*, Korean*, Malay**
short: A desktop pet game with a companion who blinks, breathes, and follows your cursor. Drag, resize, pin, lock or hide her, and pair her with static, GIF or MP4 wallpapers. Discover and share characters and wallpapers through Steam Workshop for company while you work, study or relax.
about: Keep a companion on your desktop  This is a desktop pet game. Place her in a corner of your desktop and see a familiar face whenever you look up from working, studying, browsing the web, or relaxing.  There are no schedules to complete and no need for constant attention. Keep her by your side with your favorite static or animated wallpaper, or temporarily hide her and enjoy the scenery on its own.  She blinks, breathes, and looks your way  The game includes one desktop pet character with natural blinking, breathing, and idle movements. Her head and eyes follow your cursor, while her hair and clothes sway gently with her movements.  Arrange and control her your way    Drag the character to move her. Hover over her and scroll the mouse wheel to resize her from 55% to 450%.    Switch always-on-top on or off to keep her in front of other windows or let her stay behind them.    Transparent areas around and within the character let mouse clicks pass through. Enable Lock to let mouse input pass through the entire character.    Hide the character when you need to focus, then show her again from the system tray menu. Hiding her does not stop the active animated wallpaper.    Use the right-click and system tray menus to change settings, switch characters and wallpapers, lock, show or hide the character, or exit the game. You can also show or hide the taskbar icon.    Bring your desktop scenery to life  The game includes static and animated wallpapers. Choose a gentle, still background or switch to an animated scene with drifting motes of light to bring a little movement to your desktop.    Set a local GIF animation or MP4 video as an animated wallpaper that plays behind your desktop icons.    The wallpaper selection menu brings together built-in wallpapers and downloaded, compatible Workshop wallpapers for easy switching.    Turn off the wallpaper feature to restore the desktop background recorded before you enabled it.    Animated wallpapers play while the game is running. MP4 playback depends on the video's encoding and your system's decoding support.  Discover characters and wallpapers in the Workshop  Steam Workshop has separate Character and Wallpaper categories. Explore community creations for more desktop combinations beyond the built-in content.    Browse, search, and subscribe to compatible community content. Once downloaded, select it from the corresponding menu.    Share your own compatible character packages, or upload PNG/JPG static wallpapers, GIF/MP4 animated wallpapers, and preview images.    Manage your published content by updating or deleting it.    Characters and wallpapers each have their own selection menu. Character animation depends on the resources used, and community content must use formats supported by the game.  Your desktop preferences, remembered  Character size, position, language, and display preferences are saved automatically. The game supports restoring placement across multiple monitors and adjusts it to the available screen area.  Steam Cloud can sync preferences such as character size, position, and language. You must be signed in to Steam with cloud sync enabled. Local wallpaper files and startup settings are not transferred through cloud saves.  Starting with Windows is supported and enabled by default on first use. You can turn it off in settings at any time. Only one instance of the game runs at a time to prevent duplicate launches.  Start in a familiar language  The interface supports 30 languages. On first launch, the game checks the Steam interface language first, then the game or system language if needed. You can change the language in settings at any time, and your choice is saved.  Collect a few mementos with ease  The game includes 10 Steam achievements. Use the achievement unlock option in the menu to unlock them in sequence, with no complex challenges required.  Pair your character with a favorite wallpaper and bring a little warmth and life to everyday computer time.

name: Idyll Isle
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Traditional Chinese
short: A cozy idle island sim for your desktop, in a slim window above the taskbar. Islanders of every trade farm, chop wood, fish, mine, and cook. Craft and place buildings, upgrade tools, and make the island the last livable place at sea. Then sail past the mist to rebuild five lost islands.
about: Idyll Isle runs in a slim, transparent window above your taskbar and never covers your work. While you work, study, or watch videos, the island keeps going at the bottom of the screen. A glance now and then to adjust your plans is all it takes.    The 2.0 major free update is out now, adding aid for the Veil Archipelago, island-wide power, Autumnwood Manor, and over two hundred pieces of furniture.   Islanders work on their own according to their trade: they farm, chop wood, fish, mine, and cook. You assign the work, plan where facilities go, and upgrade their tools. As the island grows, you can send expedition parties out to sea in search of collectibles, then build the Echo and sail past the Veiltide to the Veil Archipelago.          From Wheat Field to Production Chain  Start with a single wheat field and build up a full production chain. Crops and catches become meals at the Kitchen, ore is smelted into ingots and forged into tools at the Blacksmith Shop, and timber and stone bricks go into new facilities. Later on come island-wide power, Sprinklers, the Deep Drill, and the Tree Nursery, and flowers, mushrooms, and herbs can be turned into dried goods, expedition potions, and perfumes. With dozens of crops, recipes, ores, and catches, how they link into supply lines is up to you.          Build, Restore, and Expand  Buildings such as Farm Plots, Water Wells, Storage, Kitchens, Animal Pens, Blacksmith Shops, Gem Workshops, and Trading Posts can be placed anywhere on land. Layout affects efficiency: build Storage near a work area and islanders spend less time walking. Repair broken bridges, abandoned railways, and derelict facilities to open new areas with more fields, waters, and ore veins.          Tool Upgrades  Every trade has its own tools: sickles, buckets, axes, fishing rods, hammers, and spatulas. Tool quality sets work efficiency. A better sickle harvests more cleanly, and a better rod comes up empty less often. At the Blacksmith Shop, smelted ingots become new tools, from Primitive up to Advanced, with a fourth tier of Master tools later on. Accessories such as boots and gloves add further bonuses.          Animals and Trade  Wild animals appear on the island. Feed and tame them, and they move into Animal Pens to produce eggs, milk, and wool. Pair them to breed, and the offspring inherit their parents' quality. Repairing the Lighthouse opens trade routes, and Trading Post caravans carry goods out to sell and bring back the supplies you order.          Expeditions  Recruit adventurers at the Expedition Tavern, form a party, and follow the routes the Lighthouse lights up, across seven sea regions of rising danger. Compare your party's power with each sea's danger before setting out, because an underpowered party may come back empty-handed. Farther seas hold rarer finds, such as the Coastal Seashell, Weathered Compass, Abyssal Coral, and Tempest Lodestone, all recorded in the Codex, and the depths of the Veiltide also yield blueprints for Treasured furniture.          The Echo and the Veil Archipelago  Once the island prospers, the Shipyard on the shore can be put back to work. Gather Premium Boards, Sail Canvas, a Nautical Chart, and voyage supplies to build the Echo and sail past the Veiltide. Beyond it, five derelict islands remain in the Veil Archipelago, and your own island's output builds housing and facilities for them. The Freighter carries building materials, balloons carry staples and daily goods, and people adrift at sea come ashore to settle. As the islands prosper, merchants from afar return to live on your island and bring the Glass Greenhouse, Master tools, and new production lines.          The Manor and Furniture Collection  Once the last island prospers, the royal court sends you the deed and the key to Autumnwood Manor, west of the Lighthouse. The manor has one floor above ground and one below, both free to decorate. Over two hundred pieces of furniture come from blueprints bought with coins,

name: DISCIPLINE
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Greek, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Dutch, Turkish, Norwegian, Bulgarian, Finnish, Malay, Ukrainian, Russian, Swedish, Spanish - Latin America, Arabic, Indonesian, Hungarian, Korean, Czech, Danish, Vietnamese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Polish, Romanian, Thai, Catalan, Galician, Georgian, Basque, Filipino, Slovak, Slovenian, Armenian, Hindi, Hebrew, Persian, Estonian
short: DISCIPLINE is a habit tracker in the form of a luxury calendar on your desktop. A calendar that holds no value on its own — its worth exists only if you build it, day by day.
about: DISCIPLINE is a minimalist desktop calendar for keeping an unbroken daily routine. It lives as a transparent, frameless widget behind all your windows, like part of the desk itself. Set one to three daily disciplines, check them all off before 3 AM, and the day is won — marked with a hand-drawn X on the calendar. Won days in a row form a chain, and that number is the heart of the product.  The rules are strict on purpose. There are no streak freezes, and the past can never be edited: miss a day and the chain breaks. DISCIPLINE promises that the number on your desk is real — which is exactly why it comes to mean something.  Features    A transparent calendar widget that sits behind every window — always visible on the desktop, never in your way, with no taskbar icon and no stolen focus.   Set 1–3 daily disciplines, each with an optional when-and-where pledge shown beside its checkbox.   The day ends at 3:00 AM, not midnight — a check-in at 1:30 AM still counts as today.   Complete everything and the day is won: a chalk X is drawn live on the calendar, generated uniquely from the date. Consecutive wins form the chain, and days 7, 30, 100, 365 and 1000 are marked in gold forever.   No streak freezes, no repairs, no backfilling yesterday. A missed day restarts the chain — a permanent design decision.   A living flame burns behind the chain number, climbing ten stages of color as the chain grows, while the number itself is recast in ten materials from bronze to black glass. The flame leans away from your cursor, flinches when poked, and burns out in a small funeral when the chain dies.   You begin by signing a contract: your reason in one line, and your real signature drawn with the mouse. The certificate can be viewed at any time.   From 8 PM an unfinished day turns the card red. The final three hours run a countdown next to the reason you signed — in your own words.   Checking a box takes more than a click: the app asks up to four short questions before the X is written. Removing a check is instant.   Every won day earns one coin. Spend them on 27 card skins — solid colors, art prints, and glass panels your wallpaper shines through. Two skins cannot be bought at any price; they unlock only at best chains of 30 and 100.   A journal page for every day: type or draw freehand (pen, eraser, color picker, paint fill, six paper types), tear off floating note sheets that live on the desktop, and time your work with the built-in stopwatch. Pages seal read-only at 3 AM.   From 5 PM you can write tomorrow's list in advance and seal it; it arrives pre-filled the next morning. Each letter lives exactly one night.   Add optional side quests for extra tasks, and pin short promises to future dates — the morning check-in reads today's promises back to you.   A private photo feed with exactly one follower: future you. Photos posted before the day is won hang as undeveloped negatives, develop the moment you win, and stay undeveloped forever on lost days. Any month can be exported as a 1080×1920 share card drawn from your real calendar.   Optional rain for focus: real rain footage on the card, with sound that keeps playing while you work in other windows. Or fold the whole card into a tiny ember — just the flame and the number.   100% offline. No account, no telemetry, no network requests. Your entire history is one local file with three rotating backups, synced through Steam Cloud. Available in 42 languages.   Performance  DISCIPLINE is built to run 24/7 without being felt. Rendering pauses completely while the widget is covered, drops to a low frame rate when you step away, and the audio engine releases the sound device after 30 seconds of silence. There is no bundled browser — the app runs on Windows' built-in WebView2 with a thin Rust shell. Windows 10/11.

name: DeskForge - Vintage Dial Pack
lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Korean, German, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese
short: Eight antique pocket-watch faces for DeskForge's desktop clock — exposed gear trains, engraved cases, hanging bows. Skeleton movements, Roman numerals, enamel work. The biggest of the dial packs: eight faces where the others hold five, same price. Requires DeskForge.
about: An heirloom in the corner of your screen  A pocket watch was never an accessory. It was something handed down — wound by hand, kept on a chain, opened when you needed to know the hour. This pack puts eight of them on your desktop, keeping real time behind every window you have open: engraved cases, gear trains left in plain view, and the little bow at the top that the chain used to hang from.           Eight pocket-watch faces — the largest pack of the set  The other dial packs hold five faces each. This one holds eight, for the same price.     A Single Thought · Gunmetal Crimson  — gunmetal case, heart-shaped skeleton window, warm crimson glow beneath     Age of Gears · Antique Gold  — openworked gear bezel, cream dial, exposed balance wheel     Thousand Hairsprings · Bronze Openwork  — engraved bronze case, full skeleton dial, movement in plain view     Four Bastions · Onyx Steel  — dark steel filigree case, black dial, triple gold gear train     Enamel Dream · Indigo Silver  — cobalt enamel scrollwork bezel, ivory dial, skeleton centre     Copper Belfry · Roman Red  — copper case, Roman numerals, gilded rosette centre     Vine and Moonlight · Frost Silver  — engraved silver case, pearl-white dial, small skeleton aperture     Floating Gold · Rose Gold  — rose-gold engraved case, ivory dial, suspended balance wheel      How it lives on the desktop     The second hand sweeps.  It glides the way a mechanical movement does, instead of ticking once a second.     Any size you like.  Scale it freely, from a small watch in the corner to something that fills half the desktop. The artwork is drawn at high resolution, so it stays sharp all the way up.     Transparency from 30% to fully solid.  Sink it into the wallpaper, or let it hold the whole desk.     It sits at the very back.  No taskbar entry, no Alt-Tab clutter, and clicking it never steals focus from whatever you are typing in. Works across multiple monitors.     Very light on resources  — it runs all day and you hardly notice it. And it measures itself: the tray menu shows the CPU and memory it is using at this moment, so you do not have to take our word for it.      Or let all eight take turns  Pick the faces you actually like and the clock rotates through them on its own — anywhere from once a minute to once every 24 hours, half an hour by default, in order or shuffled. Eight faces make for a long rotation, and it only ever draws from faces you already own, so what comes round is your collection rather than a catalogue of things you cannot have.    Cased and bowed — which is why no strap fits  These are true pocket watches: a round case, a bow at the top, and a movement laid open beneath the skeleton dial. They were made to hang from a chain and live in a waistcoat pocket, never to be buckled onto a wrist — so there is simply nowhere on them for a strap to go.  The separate Watch Strap Pack has no effect on this pack.  If straps are what you want, they belong with the wristwatch packs — dress, pilot, diver and sport. Here the engraved case is the finished object; nothing needs to be added to it.    Other styles, other packs     Dress Dial Pack  — 5 quiet formal faces for when the desktop should just look expensive.     Pilot Dial Pack  — 5 cockpit-legible faces built around oversized numerals.     Diver Dial Pack  — 5 tool faces made to be read in a single glance.     Sport Dial Pack  — 5 high-contrast faces with chronograph energy.     Tomato Clock and Advanced Time Tools  — a Pomodoro that gets eaten as you focus, plus timer, countdown, stopwatch, alarm and a 20-zone world clock. name: QuackType 嘎嘎打字鸭
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese
short: A deadpan little duck lives on your desktop and claps along to every key you press, with a crisp mechanical-keyboard click. Ten more animals, four art styles, songs, stories and a one-tap alarm. It counts your keys, never what they were, and it asks nothing of you.
about: A small duck. It lives in the corner of your screen. It sits just above your taskbar on a fully transparent background. With every key you press, it claps a wing and you hear one clean mechanical-keyboard click. Type slowly and it gives a small clap. Type at a steady pace and it works along with you. Type fast and it slams. After a long, fast burst it looks visibly worn out for a while — and a little icon over its head means it has something to say about that. About itself, not about you.   "I'm a duck. I clap when keys go down. What the keys were is not my department."  Pick your animal        The duck is the star, but ten more live in the same panel:  cat, shiba, cow, pig, sheep, rabbit, squirrel, goldfish, slime and capybara.  They are not reskins. Each one has its own lines, its own call and its own signature move — the cat's slow blink, the cow still chewing, the rabbit's ears folding flat — and the whole interface takes on that animal's colours.          Four art styles — and every animal has all four:  pixel, geometric, doodle and paper cut-out. Want a mint duck or a pink shiba? Custom colour skins are a small text file away. It talks in four languages  English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean.  Not one shared script: every animal has its own lines, written in all four, and its own way of opening its mouth — the duck says  Quack , the cat  Meow , the shiba  Woof , the rabbit  Eep . Language is one setting in the tray menu, and whichever you pick, all eleven animals speak it. The sound of a good keyboard, on any keyboard    Ten key sounds:  blue, brown, red, black, silver, silent and cream switches — plus typewriter, wooden fish and a quack.   Key-down and key-up are separate sounds with random variations, so fast typing never sounds like a machine gun.   Five volume steps, one-click mute and a global mute hotkey.   It keeps you company           Click it and it talks.  Speech bubbles and short little chats — three exchanges at most, and it always gets the last word. There's always a curt reply option. You're allowed to be short with a duck.    It watches your cursor  and leans your way when you come close.    It dozes when you're away  and greets you when you're back. It never counts how many days you were gone.    No hunger bar, no affection meter, no login streak.  Ignore it for three weeks; nothing about it gets worse.   It sings along           Sing-along:  its mouth moves to whatever is playing on your PC — any app, any song. This runs entirely on your machine.    Songs it makes up on the spot:  offline-generated music, plus a  KTV mode  with lyrics scrolling line by line, sung by a Windows voice installed on your PC.    Stories and music (optional, online):  turn on Online features and it can play free public-domain audiobooks from LibriVox and Creative Commons music. A now-playing bubble with a draggable seek bar shows what's on.   Little things it does for you           Quick alarm:  in 5, 15 or 30 minutes, 1 or 2 hours, or a custom time. Two clicks from the tray. When it's time, it rings like a real alarm clock — even if you muted it, and it tells you that up front. Snooze for 5 minutes or tap the animal to stop it.    Today's card:  a shareable poster of your animal mid-clap with today's key count. Copy it to the clipboard or save it as a PNG (no time or machine info inside).    Counters:  today and all-time. Hide them any time.    "I'll ring. Loudly. It's the one thing I'm strict about."  Pick it up. Throw it.        Hold Ctrl+Alt and drag to move it. Let go mid-swing and it flies, bounces off the edge of the screen, lands with a squash and shakes itself off. It never leaves the screen. Out of your way when you need it    Click-through:  only the animal's own pixels catch clicks; everything around it passes straight through. Turn on  fully click-through  and even the animal stops catching clicks — handy while you game.    Hide hotkey:  one key combo and it vanishes and goes

short: These features are core to the Simplode Suite experience. The ring menu system and the quick search flyout provide a stylish and customizable platform to explore and manage all of the available utilities.
about: These features are core to the Simplode Suite experience.  The ring menu system and the quick search flyout provide a stylish and customizable platform to explore and manage all of the available utilities. This product is available natively in English, but it has automated translations for most major languages. Contents: Action Search (>_), Customize Style (🖌), Safe Mode (💥), Toggle Ring Menu (🔾), Notifications (🔔), Installation (💿), Auto Start (↻), Config File (⚙💾), Generate Documentation (?🗎*), Toggle External Input (🖦), Tray Manager (Tray), About (About), Product Registration (🔑), Logging (⚠️📜), Exit (❌︎), Reset Action Arrangement (⍟⎌), Mouse Button Combos (🖱️Combo), Super Ring (⍟), Toggle Edit Mode (✎), Related Settings (⚙), Toggle Favorite (★), Help (?), Toggle Tray (Tray), Related Settings (⚙), New Standard Window (🗔*), Resize Flyout Window (⇲), Lock Flyout Window (🔒), Move Flyout Window (⇳⬄), Toggle Flyout Window Always on Top (🗔⍏), Super Ring Associated Menu (⍟), Close Flyout Window (❌︎), Reset Action Arrangement (⍟⎌), Steam Integration (Steam), Simplode Protocol Handler (§://), Welcome (Hi), Achievements (🏆), Free Beta Features (Free Beta), Free Trial (Free Trial), Feature of the Day (Free FOTD) Action Search (>_) This is a searchable list of actions.   Before typing in a query, or after you have cleared out a query, the list will prioritize items in your favorites menu to maximize the chance that you will not even need to type anything.  Settings:  Focus Free Interactions (Default: True) If enabled, many interactions with the tool will attempt to be focus free, meaning they will not take focus away from the application you are currently using.  To do this, the feature intercepts your input at a low level and redirects it to the tool.  Support for international keyboards and IMEs may be limited for this feature.   Action Search Max Results (Default: 10) This is the maximum number of action search results which will be shown in the action search.  Keeping this low can improve the performance of the action search.   Action Search Include Unlicensed (Default: True) If enabled, action search will include actions that are not currently licensed.  This may enable you to discover useful features of Simplode Suite that you might want.  If you haven't changed your Free Select feature in the last 24 hours, any of these features will be instantly available for unlock.   Action Search Max Actions with Configs (Default: 2) The top action search results can include matching configs for easy access.  The maximum number of actions that can show configs is determined by this setting.  For example, if you set this value to 5, then the top 5 action search results can contain config results.   Action Search Max Configs Per Action (Default: 2) For action results which have configs that match your query, this is the maximum number of configs which can display for each action.  So, at its default value of 2, the tool will try to give you the two best config results.  Hopefully the result you are looking for will be ranked highest so that you will not have to open the action's menu to find it.   Action Search Results Delay Seconds (Default: 0) Performance of search results can be improved by checking less often for new results.  This is the number of seconds the tool will wait after you stop typing before it will get new results.  If you set this low enough, it will trigger between key presses and performance may suffer.   Customize Style (🖌) Customize Simplode Suite style.  Settings:  Theme (Default: Moonlight) The theme setting allows you to create, load, and delete themes for the application. Currently Available Themes: Dark, Fun, Light, Midnight, Moonlight   Panel Background (Default: #E6002B39) Changes the background color of most flyouts and indicator windows of the program.   Panel Border (Default: #9BFFFFFF) Changes the border color around most flyouts and indicator windows of the program.   Ring Background (Default: #A288A6B0)

about: Transform the Look of Your Games and Applications  StyleLens is a real-time visual effects application that changes the appearance of games, applications, or your entire display. Apply ready-made effects, create your own with the visual  Effect Graph , or write custom shaders directly in the integrated  HLSL editor .  Whether you want subtle color and lighting adjustments or a completely different visual style, StyleLens gives you the tools to customize what you see without modifying the original application.  Create Your Own Look  Use the visual  Effect Graph  to build effects by connecting nodes and adjusting parameters in real time. Experiment freely and immediately see how your changes affect the screen.  From subtle color adjustments to completely different visual styles, StyleLens gives you the tools to make games and applications look the way you want.  Full Shader Control  For advanced users, StyleLens includes an integrated  HLSL Editor .  Write and edit shader code directly inside StyleLens and create effects beyond what's possible with the visual editor.  Share Through Steam Workshop  Create your own effects with the Effect Graph and share them with the community through the  Steam Workshop .  Discover effects created by other users, experiment with new styles, and expand your StyleLens collection without having to build everything yourself.  For security and validation, direct custom HLSL code is not distributed through the Workshop.  Desktop Pets  Bring a little more life to your desktop with  Desktop Pets .  Add animated companions to your screen and let them live alongside your games, applications, and customized desktop setup.  Whether you're transforming your screen with visual effects or simply want a companion hanging around on your desktop, Desktop Pets add another layer of personalization to StyleLens.
